summary: A 1929 fire-watch site in the Yaak with its original log cabin still standing, a 1963/64 flattop tower that replaced it, staffed until 1979, now a Kootenai NF rental.

facts.design: 14x14 ft R-6-style flattop cab on a 30-foot treated timber tower with catwalk; original 1929 one-story log ground house still on site
facts.status_note: Two structures remain on the site: the 1929 log ground house and the 1963/64 tower now rented out

access.note: Open to the public as a Kootenai National Forest Recreation.gov rental; short steep hike from end of access road, combination lock requires calling the Three Rivers Ranger District ahead

visit.trail_note: Short but steep hike (about 1/4 mile per firelookout.com/rec.gov directions) from the end of a rough road; also on the Pacific Northwest National Scenic Trail

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest

events.note: First structure: a one-story log ground house used for fire detection, still standing
48-foot pole tower with 6x6 ft wood cab and catwalk added above the 1929 cabin
Recreation.gov and firelookout.com date the present 30-foot timber tower with 14x14 ft flattop cab to 1963
NHLR instead dates the present tower and an accompanying helispot to 1964; sources disagree by one year
Used for fire detection until 1979, per NHLR
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register May 12, 2000
Cabin and lookout restored and placed into the Kootenai National Forest rental system

resolved_conflicts.field: year the current tower was built
resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the present tower (and a helispot) was built in 1964; Recreation.gov and firelookout.com both say 1963. The story reports the discrepancy rather than choosing a single year, since two of three sources agree on 1963 but NHLR is otherwise the most detailed source on the site's construction sequence.

sources.title: Garver Mtn. Lookout Rental, Kootenai National Forest

evidence.supports: 1929 log ground house, 1932 48ft pole tower 6x6 cab, 1964 present 30ft timber tower 14x14 flattop cab and helispot, used until 1979, restored for 2002 rental system
evidence.quote: An impressive feature of Garver Mountain Lookout is the 1929 log ground house which is still in relatively good condition. It was supplemented three years later with a 48' pole tower with 6' x 6' wood cab and catwalk. In 1964 a helispot and the present 30' timber tower with 14' x 14' flattop cab and catwalk were constructed. Used for detection until 1979, the cabin and lookout are being restored and will be placed in the Kootenai National Forest rental system in 2002.

evidence.supports: elevation 5874 ft, fire detection since 1929, first lookout one-story log cabin still on site, current lookout built 1963, rents for up to 4, 144 sq ft 40 ft tall, furnishings, no electricity, Pacific Northwest Trail, combination lock contact info
evidence.quote: Garver Mountain Lookout has been used as an observation point for detecting forest fires since 1929. The first lookout was a one-story log cabin, which is still on the site. The current lookout was built in 1963 and is available for rent for up to four people.

evidence.supports: 1963 present 30ft treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab, restored and in rental program, listed on NHLR
evidence.quote: In 1963, the present 30' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab was built, but hasn't been staffed for many years. The cabin and tower have been restored and are available on the Recreation Rental program.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 'height_m: 1.8' field looks like an error or placeholder (1.8m is under 6 feet, implausible for any lookout tower; rec.gov says the current tower is 40 feet tall). Flagging as a possible data issue for the editor rather than a sourced correction, since no source gives a tower height in meters directly. Built-year conflict (1963 vs 1964 for the current tower) handled as the brief's note anticipated.
